philosophy: TypeSpec and JSON Schema/OpenAPI are independently authored top-level authorities. Protobuf and generators lose or reshape some facts. Those edges are listed here; anything not listed is a veto.

deltas.reason: proto3 enums require a zero value. JSON Schema and TypeSpec have no unspecified transport.
proto3 has no untyped JSON object; those fields are bytes on the transport projection.
TypeSpec uses success/error models in a union while JSON Schema uses one closed object with if/then/else. The admitted states must remain identical.
Protobuf keeps one append-only message and cannot encode conditional field presence or status ranges; adapters must run the shared semantic validator.
JSON Schema uses allOf/if/then; TypeSpec uses a union of models. Semantic arms must still match.
TypeSpec models do not emit unevaluatedProperties; closedness is per-model.
Authored JSON Schema is fail-closed with additionalProperties false. TypeSpec model openness is a reviewed representation edge.
JSON Schema constrains propertyNames; TypeSpec uses Record<string>.
Protobuf is one flattened message so field numbers stay append-only; JSON Schema variants are if/then.
